question_vi: select, poll, epoll, kqueue — tiến hoá của I/O multiplexing trong Linux/macOS?
question_en: select, poll, epoll, kqueue — the evolution of I/O multiplexing in Linux/macOS?
answer_vi:
select/poll là O(n) scan không scale; epoll (Linux) và kqueue (BSD) dùng kernel-managed event notification, O(1) per event, scale đến hàng triệu FDs; io_uring là next-gen zero-copy async I/O.

**select (POSIX):** monitor tối đa 1024 FDs (FD_SETSIZE), truyền full set mỗi syscall (O(n) scan), không biết FD nào ready phải scan toàn bộ, không scale. **poll:** tương tự select nhưng không giới hạn 1024 FDs (dùng dynamic array), vẫn O(n) scan. **epoll (Linux 2.6+):** kernel-side interest list — `epoll_create`, `epoll_ctl(ADD/MOD/DEL)`, `epoll_wait` chỉ trả về ready FDs (O(1) per event). Edge-triggered (ET) mode: notify chỉ khi state change → must drain toàn bộ; Level-triggered (LT, default): notify khi FD vẫn readable/writable → simpler. **kqueue (FreeBSD/macOS):** tổng quát hơn epoll — `kevent` struct monitor FDs, signals, timers, processes, sockets; `kevent()` syscall combine register và wait. Không phải chỉ network — có thể monitor file changes (không cần inotify riêng). **io_uring (Linux 5.1+):** next-gen async I/O — submission queue + completion queue, zero-copy, batch syscalls, giảm context switch drastically. Rust tokio, Node.js 18+ đang dần áp dụng
answer_en:
select/poll are O(n) scans that do not scale; epoll (Linux) and kqueue (BSD) use kernel-managed event notification, O(1) per event, scaling to millions of FDs; io_uring is next-gen zero-copy async I/O.

**select (POSIX):** monitors up to 1024 FDs (FD_SETSIZE), passes the full set on every syscall (O(n) scan), must scan all FDs to find which are ready — does not scale. **poll:** similar to select but without the 1024 FD limit (uses a dynamic array), still O(n) scan. **epoll (Linux 2.6+):** kernel-side interest list — `epoll_create`, `epoll_ctl(ADD/MOD/DEL)`, `epoll_wait` returns only ready FDs (O(1) per event). Edge-triggered (ET) mode: notifies only on state changes → must drain completely; Level-triggered (LT, default): notifies as long as the FD remains readable/writable → simpler to use. **kqueue (FreeBSD/macOS):** more general than epoll — the `kevent` struct monitors FDs, signals, timers, processes, and sockets; `kevent()` combines registration and waiting. Not network-only — can also monitor file changes (no separate inotify needed). **io_uring (Linux 5.1+):** next-generation async I/O — submission queue + completion queue, zero-copy, batched syscalls, drastically reduced context switches. Being adopted by Rust tokio, Node.js 18+
